title: Why Pooling and Dropout?
text:
Why Pooling and Dropout?
Two different purposes
• Pooling: reduce spatial resolution and summarize local regions.
• Dropout: regularize the network by randomly dropping activations
during training.
Key distinction
Pooling changes the feature-map shape; Dropout usually preserves the shape.

title: Default CNN Stack
text:
Default CNN Stack
Typical block
Conv →(Norm) →Activation →(Pool) →(Dropout)
Interpretation
• Conv: extracts local features.
• Pool: reduces spatial size.
• Dropout: reduces overfitting during training.
Takeaway
Pooling is mainly about spatial summarization; Dropout is mainly about
regularization.

title: Max Pooling
text:
Max Pooling
Definition
Max pooling takes the maximum value inside each local window:
Yb,c,i,j =
max
(u,v)∈Ri,j
Xb,c,u,v
Intuition
• Keeps the strongest local response.
• Common after activation functions such as ReLU.
• Useful when feature presence matters more than exact location.
Takeaway
Max pooling answers: “Is this feature strongly present in this local region?”

Takeaway
Pooling changes feature-map geometry but does not add learnable parameters.

Pooling and Receptive Field
Single pooling layer
For:
Pool(k = 2, s = 2)
each output value depends on a:
2 × 2
region of the input feature map.
Effect
• Pooling increases the effective receptive field of later layers.
• Stride increases the spacing between neighboring output values.
Takeaway
Pooling is not learnable but it changes how later layers see the input

title: Dropout: Key Idea
text:
Dropout: Key Idea
Purpose
Dropout is a regularization technique. During training, it randomly sets some
activations to zero.
Informal formula
Y = M ⊙X
where M is a random mask and ⊙denotes element-wise multiplication.
Takeaway
Dropout forces the network not to rely too strongly on specific activations.

title: Dropout Probability
text:
Dropout Probability
Drop probability
Let p be the probability of dropping an activation:
p = Pr(activation is set to 0)
Keep probability
1 −p
Example
If p = 0.5, roughly half of the activations are dropped during training.
Takeaway
Larger p means stronger regularization, but too large p can hurt learning.

title: Dropout: Train vs Eval
text:
Dropout: Train vs Eval
Training mode
• Random mask is sampled.
• Some activations are set to zero.
• Remaining activations are scaled.
Evaluation mode
• Dropout is disabled.
• All activations are kept.
• The layer behaves like an identity map.
Takeaway
Dropout behaves differently in training and evaluation.

title: Dropout vs Dropout2d
text:
Dropout vs Dropout2d
Standard Dropout
Randomly drops individual elements:
Xb,c,h,w
Spatial Dropout / Dropout2d
Randomly drops entire channels for each sample:
Xb,c,:,:
Takeaway
For CNN feature maps, Dropout2d often makes more sense than element-wise
dropout because spatial positions within a channel are correlated.

title: Where to Put Dropout in CNNs?
text:
Where to Put Dropout in CNNs?
Common placements
• After fully connected layers.
• After convolutional blocks, especially in small datasets.
• Before the classifier head.
Caution
Heavy dropout inside early convolutional layers may remove too much
low-level information.
Takeaway
Dropout is useful, but its position and probability should be chosen carefully.

title: Important: Training vs Evaluation
text:
Important: Training vs Evaluation
Pooling
• Same behavior in training and evaluation.
• Deterministic operation.
Dropout
• Training: randomly drops activations.
• Evaluation: disabled, behaves like identity.
Takeaway
Pooling is always active; Dropout is active only during training.

title: PyTorch: Validation Discipline
text:
PyTorch: Validation Discipline
Correct validation pattern
model.eval ()
with
torch.no_grad ():
y = model(x)
Why?
• model.eval() disables Dropout randomness.
• It also switches BatchNorm to running statistics.
Takeaway
For models with Dropout or BatchNorm, always use model.eval() during
validation and inference.

title: Summary: Dropout
text:
Summary: Dropout
What dropout does
• Randomly removes activations during training.
• Reduces overfitting.
• Preserves tensor shape.
• Adds no learnable parameters.
Final insight
Dropout = training-time stochastic regularization.

title: Final Comparison
text:
Final Comparison
Memory rule
• Pooling: changes spatial size, no training/eval difference.
• Dropout: keeps shape, but changes behavior between training and
evaluation.
Practical rule
Use pooling to control spatial resolution; use dropout to control overfitting.
